title: "Drive on Start + Void"
description: "Native Drive Worker profiles, the sealed Cloudflare artifact, and the cutover and Vercel rollback packet."
updatedAt: "2026-11-23"

Drive (`apps/drive`) runs on TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void behind
[`@tuturuuu/start-bridge`](/build/devops/start-bridge). The Next.js build
(`build:legacy`) and the Vercel project stay in place until the cutover has been
stable, so the canonical host keeps a one-step route back.

## Worker profiles

| Profile | Selected by | Worker | Vars |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Staging (default) | no profile variable | the staging Worker name | `src/start-candidate/staging-policy.ts`; the build refuses a non-staging value |
| Production | `VITE_DRIVE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production` | `tuturuuu-drive` | `cloudflare/production-profile.json` |

The script policy comes from the bridge's nonce CSP (`strict-dynamic`) and is
enforced in both profiles. The production profile sets
`TTR_TRUSTED_TYPES_DRIVE=report`, which the bridge reads: Trusted Types reports
violations without blocking. The Worker refuses a production request whose
bindings differ from this file, so it answers 503 when the var is missing or
different. Enforcing Trusted Types is a reviewed profile change to `enforce`,
made after a signed-in crawl of every Drive route shows zero violations, and it
ships before `tuturuuu.com/drive` is mounted. The profile carries no `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX` or
`TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_DRIVE`: the response policy always sends `noindex`, and the apex
mount is served from the profile alone.

Neither profile declares routes, custom domains, `workers_dev` or
`preview_urls`. The hostname is attached at cutover by the release operator.

The production Worker answers every request with a refusal until
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`,
`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` and `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` are present
(`cloudflare/required-bindings.ts`). The Supabase origin is a public production
var pinned in `cloudflare/production-profile.json`, like Finance's; the other
three are Worker secrets. Names only are recorded here; secret values stay in the
secret store. A production request whose Supabase origin differs from the pinned
one answers 503. The production profile admits `drive.tuturuuu.com` and the
exact `/drive` mount and its descendants on `tuturuuu.com`. Both use the
production configuration fence. The staging profile admits only its declared
staging hostname, and unlisted hosts or apex paths answer `404`.

## Build and artifact

`drive-cloudflare-artifact.yaml` runs on `ready-for-ci` pull requests and by
manual dispatch. It builds with `bun run --cwd apps/drive build:cloudflare`,
checks the route registry, tests, types and lint, and stamps the exact source
commit into the output. The emitted Worker runs in workerd on both production
hosts. On manual dispatch CI seals the route-free archive with
`scripts/ci/drive-native-artifact.py` and repeats the same runtime suite against
a clean restore before uploading `drive-native-<source SHA>` (7 days).

Do not run `build:cloudflare` on a shared development machine; use the workflow.

### Wave-1 producer

`wave1-native-production.yaml` releases Drive through the same producer as the
other wave-1 apps (`app=drive`). With `release-artifact` and the exact `main`
`source-sha` it builds the workspace suppliers and the production Void profile,
runs `drive-native-artifact.py config` and `cutover.runtime.mjs` on the emitted
Worker, seals the route-free bytes (`workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off, no
routes) with the profile in `scripts/ci/wave1-native-profiles.json`, and requalifies
the restored archive without provider credentials. The recipe's vars equal
`cloudflare/production-profile.json`; change the two together. The release inputs and
the recipe's public input pin both name the production Supabase origin. The runtime
gates (`cutover.runtime.mjs` on the emitted build, `wave1-native-runtime.mjs` on the
restored archive) also require, on `drive.tuturuuu.com` and `tuturuuu.com/drive`, an
enforcing nonce and `'strict-dynamic'` `Content-Security-Policy` on an owned HTML
response and `require-trusted-types-for` only in `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`. The publish job does not run for a release artifact,
and production publication stays held until an explicit cutover change admits Drive.

## Cutover packet

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-drive` |
| Routes | Existing canonical subdomain, plus `/drive` and `/drive/*` via the gateway's `MOUNT_DRIVE` binding after acceptance |
| Static assets binding | `ASSETS` (`dist/client`, `run_worker_first`) |
| Build command | `VITE_DRIVE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production bun run --cwd apps/drive build:cloudflare` |
| Secrets (names) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` |
| Pinned public var | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` (the production origin, in `cloudflare/production-profile.json`) |
| Central API origin | `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN=https://tuturuuu.com` |
| Rollback | Capture the Worker, version and hostname attachment that serve `drive.tuturuuu.com` before the first change (it currently serves an older vinext build), plus the active gateway version, mount bindings, Web's active-mount list and overlapping zone routes for the apex. The [ordered reverse rollback](#rollback) uses these captures |
| Data | no database writes and no migrations |

### Switch

Drive's production publication is held until the release authority admits it.
The hostname `drive.tuturuuu.com` is attached to the legacy `tuturuuu-drive`
Worker, and the publish preflight refuses while it stays attached there, so the
hostname moves first. Each step is verified before the next one starts, and each
has the reverse step listed under [Rollback](#rollback).

1. **Record** the source SHA, the sealed artifact name, the Vercel deployment ID
   and the captures listed in the packet.
2. **1a, move the hostname.** Reattach `drive.tuturuuu.com` to the
   `tuturuuu-apex-redirect` Worker with `drive` *not* in `SUBDOMAIN_REDIRECT_APPS`.
   With no redirect list entry the Worker is a pure passthrough to its `APP_DRIVE`
   binding for `tuturuuu-drive`, so the legacy build keeps serving unchanged while
   the hostname leaves that Worker's attachment. The redirect Worker needs that
   binding (a gateway configuration change) before this step.
3. **Publish native Drive** with `TTR_TRUSTED_TYPES_DRIVE=report`. Provision the
   three Worker secrets on `tuturuuu-drive` first, publish the sealed route-free
   artifact, and record the vinext preimage version that the upload replaces.
4. **1b, signed-in crawl.** Crawl every Drive route signed in through a
   `Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides` staged version of the new Worker. The
   expected result is zero Trusted Types violations in the report endpoint's logs.
5. **1c, enforce.** Change the profile to `enforce`, re-release through the
   producer and publish the new sealed version.
6. **2, mount.** Write the gateway mount for `/drive` and `/drive/*`
   (`MOUNT_DRIVE`) and, in the same window, land the matching mount commit on
   `main` so Web's active-mount list includes `drive`. Run
   `node scripts/active-app-mounts.mjs --live <version.json>` against the live
   gateway version before any Web family promotion, and keep unrelated gateway
   and Web changes frozen until it passes.
7. **3, redirect.** Add `drive` to `SUBDOMAIN_REDIRECT_APPS` so
   `drive.tuturuuu.com` navigations answer 301 to `tuturuuu.com/drive`.

Run private version-pinned smoke for both production host variants before routing
traffic to a new version, and the smoke below after each step that changes
routing.

### Smoke

```bash
# Anonymous protected route redirects to /login; no 5xx
curl -sI https://drive.tuturuuu.com/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 | head -5
# Login page renders
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://drive.tuturuuu.com/login
# Build identity matches the accepted SHA
curl -s https://drive.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
# Foreign host is refused
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: untrusted.invalid' https://drive.tuturuuu.com/login
```

Check the bare apex mount with duplicate query keys, a Vietnamese deep link,
and the exact build identity on both hosts. Signed-out protected pages
redirect to the central login with the correct app verifier and complete
return query. The public Start 404 under the verifier prefix emits loadable
CSS and scripts on both hosts. Unauthenticated storage access returns 401,
and the mounted app-session mint endpoint returns 409.

With a fleet account and disposable workspace data, check root sessions,
workspace isolation, signed upload and download, byte ranges, previews, API
fallback, and unzip continuity. The local Worker fixtures verify delegated
storage request bodies, ranges and response status.

### Rollback

- **Triggers:** roll back immediately on a smoke, authentication, error-rate,
  latency or storage permission regression during the 30–60 minute watch.
- **Order:** undo only the steps that were completed, newest first. Check
  `drive.tuturuuu.com` and `tuturuuu.com/drive` after each reverse step before
  taking the next.

1. Remove `drive` from `SUBDOMAIN_REDIRECT_APPS` and release that Worker version;
   the hostname returns to passthrough and the 301 stops.
2. Reattach `drive.tuturuuu.com` to the Worker it was attached to, from the
   capture taken before step 1a.
3. Revert the mount commit on `main` and rebuild Web's active-mount list with
   `drive` removed, preserving the other entries.
4. Restore the captured gateway version at 100%, using the
   [gateway rollback procedure](/build/devops/gateway-worker#one-action-rollback-for-a-gateway-mount).
   `/drive` and `/drive/*` return to their captured dispatch.
5. Restore the Worker preimage: the recorded vinext version of `tuturuuu-drive`.
   Roll the Trusted Types profile back to `report` first when only the `enforce`
   release regressed, because that is a one-var change to a published version.

- **Data:** a route rollback changes no stored files or metadata.
- **Stability:** keep the Vercel project and domain for 14 consecutive stable
  days before decommissioning, which is a separate approval.

## Legacy hostname

`drive.tuturuuu.com` moves to the
[legacy redirect Worker](/build/devops/gateway-worker#legacy-subdomain-redirect)
at step 1a, before the native publish, because the publish preflight refuses a
Worker that still holds a route or custom domain. With `APP_DRIVE` bound and
`drive` absent from `SUBDOMAIN_REDIRECT_APPS`, the redirect Worker forwards every
request to `tuturuuu-drive`, so `tuturuuu-drive` keeps serving the hostname.
Adding `drive` to the list is a separate, later step, taken after the apex mount
passes signed-in smoke. Once enabled, check
that `/vi/personal?ref=a&ref=b` redirects once to
`/drive/vi/personal?ref=a&ref=b`, and that legacy API requests, auth callbacks and
assets still reach Drive. Restore the captured attachment first if rolling back
after enabling the 301.

Drive needs no `/vi/drive` locale alias at the gateway: Drive owns `NEXT_LOCALE`,
and `tuturuuu.com/vi/drive` already answers `307` to `/drive` with
`NEXT_LOCALE=vi` set.

## Latency qualification

Compare cold starts and warmed requests separately for the same route mix.
The Worker serves fingerprinted Vite assets with immutable caching. HTML,
auth redirects and signed-in API responses keep their private cache policy.
The Drive page and layout share a workspace read and its actor resolution
within the Start request. Include the dashboard, workspace permissions and
signed-in storage in the hosted watch.
